Case built to train nodule detection and classification: the underlying CT is real and normal (LIDC-IDRI archive), the four nodules were added by computer with partial volume and noise of the original image. The realism is good but not perfect: the appearance of margins and spicules is simplified.
Method: scroll through the whole volume in the lung window, possibly with thick-slab MIP; follow every round image through the neighboring slices (a vessel continues, a nodule appears and disappears). Measure in the lung window: mean of long and short axis, rounded to the millimeter; in part-solid nodules also measure the solid component.
Fleischner 2017 (incidental nodules, adults ≥ 35 years, not screening, not oncologic): with multiple nodules, manage the most suspicious. Solid > 8 mm: CT at 3 months, PET-CT or sampling. Part-solid ≥ 6 mm: CT at 3-6 months; if it persists and the solid component is ≥ 6 mm it is highly suspicious. Pure ground glass ≥ 6 mm: CT at 6-12 months, then every 2 years until 5 years. Solid 6-8 mm: CT at 6-12 months (high risk: also 18-24 months). In a screening program Lung-RADS is used instead.
Più noduli: classifica tutti, gestisci i: Multiple nodules: classify all, manage the most suspicious. In part-solid nodules the solid component counts.
